replacements.text: The acceptance-criteria standard has a coverage rule that asks whether each commitment has a criterion. The `verification-contract` rule (the rule that judges the check each criterion names) opened with the same question, so its reviewer filed coverage gaps under it. Now that rule asks only about each criterion's check, while the coverage rule asks whether a commitment has a criterion. The corrected control document returns an empty report in 9 of 10 panel runs, up from 2 of 10. All 10 runs on the defective document still object to the planted criterion.

The `verification-contract` rule (the rule that judges each criterion's check) opened with the coverage rule's question. It now judges each criterion's check and leaves the question of whether a commitment has a criterion to coverage.
The attack skill's reviewer table gains a column stating what each reviewer reads, which determines who owns each rule.
